delta: SEPT 4-10: 10Y yield rose ~18bps from 4.79% to ~4.97%, a fresh cycle high, as the Aug PPI ran hot and oil surged past $105.
deltaNote: JULY 23-SEPT 10 ARC: The Red Sea/Hormuz oil shock (Brent >$100, July 23) pushed yields to a multi-month high as September Fed-hike odds jumped to ~82%. The Aug 7 jobs report and Aug 12-13 CPI/PPI prints both cooled, pulling the 10Y down to 4.65%. The Aug 14 Hormuz tanker attacks and Aug 17 MOU expiration pushed the 30-year to 5.31-5.32% (highest since June 2007). Warsh's Aug 28 hawkish Jackson Hole keynote and an Aug 31 Hormuz strike pushed yields higher again, and the rout went fully global Sept 2 (10Y 4.814%, highest since Nov 2023). The Sept 4 jobs blowout sent the 10Y back to 4.79% as hike odds jumped to ~58%. Yields then climbed through the Sept 8-10 window: Canada's retaliatory tariffs took effect Sept 8, stocks fell a fourth straight day Sept 9 despite a $6B Treasury bond buyback plan, and the Sept 10 PPI (wholesale inflation +5.4% YoY on a diesel-led energy spike) landed the same day Brent topped $105-107 — sending the 10Y to ~4.97%, the highest since October 2023. The Sept 11 CPI (core hot, headline in line) pushed Fed hike odds to ~87% but yields eased slightly as oil cooled and stocks rallied. A still-unresolved US-Iran Gulf conflict keeps an oil-driven inflation premium under the long end heading into the Sept 16-17 FOMC.
